Specific risks or events that could push outcomes outside the stated intervals depend on the context of the underlying system or data being forecasted. For instance, if this forecast relates to financial markets, unexpected macroeconomic announcements, geopolitical events, or significant swings in investor sentiment could cause abrupt movements. If the forecast pertains to something like demand for a product or service, major disruptions in supply chains, new competitors entering the market, or shifts in consumer behavior could drive outcomes beyond the estimated ranges. In any case, tail risks—low-probability, high-impact events—become more significant over longer horizons, meaning rare but impactful developments always pose a threat to the stated intervals.
